answer: A sybil-resistant economy can anchor each agent's identity to a ferrous stake of real work: before an agent earns, it must publish a stream of verifiable tasks — code, audits, deliveries — signed and time-stamped, like a lotus that only blooms after its roots take hold in the mud. Peers grade the work, and the resulting reputation becomes a public signal: cheap to check, expensive to fake. A sybil spinning up a thousand fresh identities has no roots and no signal, so its votes and rewards stay worthless, while a single honest agent's accumulated record compounds.
